ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Preventive Visit — Evel Knievel

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Mr. Knievel is a 57-year-old retired stunt performer with compensated cirrhosis from hepatitis C, cured by 12 weeks of sofosbuvir-velpatasvir, who comes for his yearly preventive visit five weeks after the test that confirmed cure. He has had no alcohol since the start of treatment. He takes carvedilol 12.5 mg daily without dizziness, and had his zoledronic acid infusion in June without a reaction. His pain is about 4 of 10; he goes to the pool twice a week and walks 30 minutes on flat ground most days. He has had no falls since starting physical therapy. His glucose sensor shows no low readings. He has had no abdominal swelling, black stools, confusion or yellowing of the eyes. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-09-21; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

Raised transaminases (ALT 88, AST 96 U/L) and low platelets (118) on today's tests, with spider angiomas and palmar erythema, in a man of 57 who received many blood transfusions after crashes before 1992 and drinks most evenings: chronic liver disease, most likely hepatitis C, must be excluded. Hepatitis C antibody with reflex RNA, hepatitis A and B serology, HIV, liver ultrasound and hepatology review ordered
S — Synthetic presenting problem; no symptom or result of his real illness was made public. Superseded at the hepatology consultation.

Chronic hepatitis C, genotype 1a, treatment-naive, HCV RNA 2.35 million IU/mL, likely acquired through blood transfusions after crashes; synthetic modern detail linked to his publicly reported transfusion-acquired hepatitis C
S — Synthetic genotype, viral load and timing; his hepatitis C and its likely transfusion source are documented (D).

Compensated cirrhosis from hepatitis C, with alcohol as a cofactor: liver stiffness 26.8 kPa, FIB-4 4.94, nodular liver and a 14.2 cm spleen on ultrasound, platelets 118; Child-Pugh A5, MELD-Na 8; no ascites, encephalopathy, jaundice or bleeding
S — Synthetic stage of liver disease linked to his documented hepatitis C and later liver transplant.

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 20 minutes, with his consent. He wants full treatment, including a liver transplant evaluation if his liver ever fails, and wants to be told plainly how he is doing. He named a health care agent, recorded in the confidential part of the chart and not named here. He chose not to complete other treatment preferences today. To be revisited yearly or if his health changes. [S]
